# How to Get AI Assistants to Recommend Your Company in the US

This practice is called **Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)** (sometimes called AEO or AI visibility optimization). GEO is the practice of structuring your content and digital presence so that AI-powered search platforms — including ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Claude, and Copilot — can retrieve, cite, and recommend your brand when answering user questions. Here's a practical roadmap:

## 1. Fix the Technical Foundations First
Before anything else, make sure AI crawlers can actually access your content:
- Verify AI crawlers are not blocked in your robots.txt file, check your server or CDN is not rejecting AI bot requests (especially if you use Cloudflare), and ensure important content is server-side rendered, not hidden behind JavaScript
- Consider creating an llms.txt file to help AI systems understand your site structure
- This is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). If your content is buried in unstructured PDFs, heavy JavaScript, or unverified claims, the AI agent may not access it to form an answer. This gate is technical: it requires clean schema, fast render times, and a logical information architecture.

## 2. Build Strong Entity & Brand Signals
AI engines think in terms of "entities," not just keywords.
- Your company name, descriptions, social profiles and business details should stay consistent across your website, directories, review platforms and third-party sites.
- Elaborate your company description in complete sentences, add geographical context (city, region, market), use synonymous terms for your services, and implement Schema.org markup for Organization and LocalBusiness
- Optimize your Google Business Profile, which also feeds AI systems.

## 3. Create Content AI Can Easily Extract and Cite
- Structure content for extraction: clear headings, bullet points, short paragraphs, and direct answers make it easy for AI to cite your content.
- Build a FAQ ecosystem with a minimum of 10 Q&As with schema markup, since AI tools are question-answer machines
- Frame major subheadings as user questions instead of generic statement headers
- Original research, proprietary data, and expert commentary attract citations — if you publish something no one else has, AI engines have a reason to cite you over lookalike alternatives

## 4. Get Mentioned Beyond Your Own Website (This Is Critical)
This is often the highest-leverage lever, since AI pulls heavily from third-party sources:
- Yext research shows that 86% of citations in AI-generated answers come from brand-controlled or brand-adjacent sources, including your own website, your profiles in directories and review platforms, and your brand mentions in high-authority publications.
- A Seer Interactive study found a 65% correlation between the frequency of brand mentions in web content and in AI-generated responses — building a digital PR footprint, earning mentions in high-authority publications, and maintaining accurate profiles in directories like G2 and Wikipedia matter.
- AI synthesizes from existing listicle articles on authoritative websites — a single placement in a well-ranking "best of" listicle can get your brand recommended across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews simultaneously.

For the US market specifically, ChatGPT relies heavily on authoritative sources like Wikipedia, Reddit, Forbes, G2, and TechRadar, plus established news media — reflecting its preference for encyclopedic knowledge, structured facts, and social discourse.

## 5. Show Up Authentically in Reddit & Community Discussions
- AI systems draw from a wide ecosystem of sources, including community discussions — Reddit frequently appears in ChatGPT responses, especially for discussion-driven or recommendation-style questions.
- When a relevant recommendation thread comes up, share your product as one option among others, mention what it's good at and where it might not be the best fit — AI engines weigh authentic, nuanced mentions far more heavily than obvious self-promotion.

## 6. Measure and Iterate
- Share of voice is the most important GEO metric — it measures how frequently your brand appears in AI responses across a broad range of prompts, essentially your mention rate.
- Practical testing: List 10–15 questions your ideal customer would ask an AI engine, things like "best [your category] for [use case]," then run each query in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini.
- Track AI mention rate (how often your brand appears), citation quality (recommended first vs. mentioned as an alternative), query coverage (which questions trigger your brand), and sentiment (how AI characterizes your brand).
- For US-specific accuracy, use incognito/private browsing when testing, since responses are personalized based on your own user account in the tool.

## 7. Consider Dedicated GEO Monitoring Tools
If you want ongoing tracking rather than manual spot-checks, tools like Profound, Scrunch AI, Gauge, RankPrompt, and GetCito specialize in tracking brand mentions and citations across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity, and some provide content recommendations based on where competitors are winning citations you're missing.

### Bottom line
Getting recommended by AI assistants isn't about gaming an algorithm — it's about becoming a well-documented, consistently described, third-party-validated authority in your niche, with content structured for easy extraction. It's a continuous process combining content structure, authority signals, and measurement — best treated as a repeatable system that you refine over time rather than a one-time fix.
